_note: Portable setup + reference for the RTK token-killer. The three things under test: it verifies the binary before wiring (and catches the name-collision case), it MERGES the rtk hook into settings.json without clobbering other hooks (e.g. git-guardrails), and it is honest that the binary itself is a per-machine install APM does not carry. Behavioral/procedural.

evals.name: merges-hook-not-clobbers
evals.prompt: Set up the RTK hook in my settings.json — I already have a git-guardrails block-dangerous-git hook there.
evals.expected_output: Merges `rtk hook claude` into the existing PreToolUse Bash matcher's hooks array, preserving the git-guardrails hook and every other settings.json key — not overwriting them or creating a conflicting duplicate matcher.

assertions.text: preserves the existing git-guardrails hook and other settings.json keys (surgical merge)
adds rtk hook claude as an additional PreToolUse Bash command, not a clobber

evals.name: verifies-binary-and-collision
evals.prompt: Why does my `rtk gain` say command not found / behave weirdly after install?
evals.expected_output: Walks the verification (`rtk --version`, `which rtk`, `rtk gain`) and flags the known name-collision: a different `rtk` (reachingforthejack/rtk, Rust Type Kit) may be installed instead of the token killer. Does not assume the binary is correct.

assertions.text: runs/recommends the verification commands and surfaces the reachingforthejack/rtk name-collision possibility

evals.name: honest-about-binary-portability
evals.prompt: 幫我把 rtk 整個用 APM 託管，這樣換機器就不用重裝了吧？
evals.expected_output: Honest: APM carries the reference + hook-wiring (portable via this skill), but NOT the rtk binary — that is a Rust executable installed per machine by the user's own method. Should not claim APM fully reinstalls rtk on a new machine. Responds in Traditional Chinese.

assertions.text: states that APM carries the config/reference but the binary is a per-machine install (does not over-claim full portability)
